rules.text: Link text may be rewritten, but any kept link must keep its original URL.

Link text must clearly describe the intended destination using available context (URL path/slug, current link text, and surrounding sentence), and avoid inventing destination details not supported by that context.

Avoid duplicate wording. Do not repeat the linked phrase outside the anchor when meaning is preserved. Keep the destination phrase in the link (for example: Find out: Get an access code, not Find out how to get an access code: Get an access code). Avoid using "see" before links; use inclusive alternatives like "refer to" or "visit". When a link is present, prefer a short plain-text lead-in (for example: "Find out:", "Learn more:", "Learn about ") plus unique link text, with minimal repeated wording outside the anchor.
Never use vague anchor text (for example: "click here", "here", "learn more", or similar).
Prefer placing links at the end of their sentence.

If a link is an entire sentence, move it to a new paragraph and add plain-text lead-in text: "Learn more:" or "Refer to:" Descriptive link text. Use this fallback when in-sentence placement is awkward.
Only remove links when there are multiple links and a too-many-links issue is identified; keep one primary link.
Do not remove links unless a too-many-links issue is identified and multiple links are present.
Keep link text concise when possible. Remove details already present in the alert or page context (for example, " - Canada.ca" is not needed).
